questions.question: When you see a drawbridge with a traffic signal, you may go across when:

options.text: You stop 50 feet before the bridge.
Other vehicles are also going across.
You get out and check the conditions first.

questions.correctAnswerText: The signal is green.
questions.explanation: When the traffic signal shows green, you can slow down and go across the drawbridge without stopping.

questions.question: When driving in fog and you see lights ahead, you should know:

options.text: The lights are on the road.
The lights may be a reflection.
The lights may be an optical illusion.
The lights may not show where the road is—a vehicle may have left the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lights may not show where the road is—a vehicle may have left the road.
questions.explanation: In fog, lights are not a reliable guide to where the road is. A vehicle showing lights may have driven off the road.

questions.question: You can identify a vehicle with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) by:

options.text: A sticker on the control panel.
A yellow warning light on the dashboard.
The letters "ABS" on the brake pedal.
A metal plate inside the driver's door.

questions.correctAnswerText: A yellow warning light on the dashboard.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle has ABS if it has a yellow ABS warning light on the dashboard.

questions.question: Driver fatigue:
questions.correctAnswerText: Can make driving unsafe.
questions.explanation: Driving while tired is dangerous and increases crash risk. Take steps before your trip to avoid driving tired.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should NOT:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up.
questions.explanation: If you must drive in fog, slow down and use low beam headlights and fog lights. Turn on hazard lights. Do not speed up.

questions.question: Speeding:

options.text: Is a major cause of fatal crashes.
Is a good way to arrive quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a major cause of fatal crashes.
questions.explanation: Speeding causes many fatal crashes. Never drive faster than the speed limit. Adjust your speed to match conditions.

questions.question: Steering wheel play should not be more than:
questions.correctAnswerText: 10 degrees.
questions.explanation: More than 10 degrees of steering wheel play (about 2 inches of movement on a 20-inch wheel) makes steering difficult.

questions.question: When shifting gears, what happens if you stay in neutral too long?

options.text: You may have trouble shifting to the next gear.
The vehicle will be hard to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have trouble shifting to the next gear.
questions.explanation: Staying in neutral too long when shifting can make it hard to move into the next gear.

questions.question: Before a bus goes into a curve, the driver should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Crashes on curves often happen because drivers go too fast. Bus drivers should always slow down before entering a curve, turn, on-ramp, or off-ramp.

questions.question: Rims that have been welded to repair damage:

options.text: Are safe when carrying heavy loads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are unsafe.
questions.explanation: Check your wheels before driving for damage. Wheels or rims that have been welded are not safe to use.

questions.question: How do you warn drivers behind you that you are slowing down?

options.text: Turn on the right turn signal, then the left turn signal.
Tap your brake pedal a few times to flash the brake lights.
Swerve from side to side to get attention.
Turn all lights on and off several times.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tap your brake pedal a few times to flash the brake lights.
questions.explanation: To alert drivers behind you, tap your brake pedal lightly a few times. This makes your brake lights flash.

questions.question: Which one does NOT help prevent drowsiness while driving?

options.text: Driving during hours when you would normally be asleep

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving during hours when you would normally be asleep
questions.explanation: Driving while tired is very dangerous. Good strategies include getting full sleep before a trip, having someone ride with you to share driving, driving during hours when you are normally awake, and avoiding drowsy medications.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the parking brake.
questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when you leave your vehicle.

questions.question: Hydraulic brakes can fail for two reasons. Which is one of them?

options.text: There is a loss of hydraulic pressure.
The brakes are used too much in one day.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a loss of hydraulic pressure.
questions.explanation: Hydraulic brake failure usually happens for two reasons: brakes fade from overuse on a downgrade, or there is a loss of hydraulic pressure. Well-maintained brakes rarely fail, but you should know what to do if they do.

questions.question: What are multi-speed axles and auxiliary transmissions used for?

options.text: To make a vehicle run more smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: To provide extra gears.
questions.explanation: Many vehicles use multi-speed rear axles and auxiliary transmissions to provide extra gears. They are usually controlled by a selector knob on the gearshift lever.

questions.question: If you feel sleepy while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Keep driving to finish the trip.
Drive faster to reach your destination sooner.
Leave the road and take a nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave the road and take a nap.
questions.explanation: If you feel sleepy while driving, stop and get sleep. Trying to fight exhaustion is dangerous and causes many fatal crashes. Stimulants may keep you awake but will not make you more alert. When stimulants wear off, you will be even more tired than before.

questions.question: When checking a power steering system, make sure that:

options.text: The fluid is at the proper level.
The hoses are connected to the battery.

questions.correctAnswerText: The fluid is at the proper level.
questions.explanation: When checking power steering, inspect the hoses, pumps, and fluid level. Look for leaks and repair them before driving.

questions.question: If your load is too long during a pre-trip check, what should you do?

options.text: Cut the length of the load.
Make sure flags and lights for the oversize load are fastened securely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure flags and lights for the oversize load are fastened securely.
questions.explanation: If a pre-trip check shows your load is oversize, make sure all required signs, flags, lamps, and reflectors are properly mounted and that you have all required permits.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact with the driver.
Assume the other driver does not see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume the other driver does not see you.
questions.explanation: When passing a pedestrian or another vehicle, assume they do not see you.

questions.question: What is true about over-the-counter medication?

options.text: It poses no safety risks to drivers.
It is not covered by driving under the influence laws.
It can affect your ability to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can affect your ability to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter medications can have side effects that impair your driving ability. It is illegal to drive while under the influence of alcohol or any controlled substance, including some over-the-counter medications.
